newsitem.title: USA: Morrison named to succeed Johnson at Campbell.
newsitem.headline: Morrison named to succeed Johnson at Campbell.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co. said Monday it named Dale Morrison to succeed David Johnson as president and chief executive officer of the soup and prepared foods company.
Johnson, 64, will remain chairman of the board and its executive committee until his retirement on July 31, 1998, Campbell said.

Morrison, 48, is president of Campbell's International and Speciality Foods division. He joined the company in June 1995 as president of the Pepperidge Farm division. Under his leadership, Pepperidge Farm's annual sales growth rate rose from about 2 percent to nearly 13 percent this year. His approach is now being carried out across the entire company, Campbell said.

"My priority is to ensure that we continue our relentless commitment to building shareowner wealth," Johnson said in a written statement. "I will assist Dale in exploring the strategies needed to achieve Campbell's vision of becoming the best consumer products company in the world."
The process of finding a successor to Johnson began last year with the appointment of a special committee of independent directors.

Campbell also announced the promotion of two other executives. Chief Financial Officer Basil Anderson and U.S. Grocery division president Robert Bernstock were named executive vice presidents. They had been senior vice presidents.
Campbell's stock was off 25 cents at $49.125 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
